Doctoral Program at Freie Universität
Doctoral Program in Physics - Creating fundamentals for future innovations
Around 180 doctoral students study and work at the Department of Physics. Every year, about 40 physicists earn their PhD at Freie Universität Berlin.
If you are interested in pursuing a doctoral degree, please contact the research group that best matches your research interests directly.
PhD Program Structure
1 topic
1 supervisor
1 written doctoral thesis
1 disputation
Doctoral students are usually employed as scientific staff in the research group (AG) where they pursue their doctorate.
Doctoral Thesis
The dissertation can be submitted as either a monograph or a cumulative dissertation consisting of at least four publications with the doctoral candidate as first author.
On the day of submission, at least one* printed, bound copy of the dissertation and one digital version (PDF) must be submitted to the PhD Program Office via email or a cloud link.
* Before submitting your dissertation, please check with your supervisors whether they would like a paper version. If so, you may need to increase the number of printed copies to be submitted.
Obligatory parts of a thesis are:
Title page (draft)
Summary in German and English (maximum one page)
Declaration of authorship (draft)
Disputation
The disputation allows the doctoral student to demonstrate their presentation skills and ability to engage in scientific discussions.
30 minutes of presentation
30 to 60 minutes of discussion with the members of the PhD Examination Committee.
The disputation is open to the public: Interested persons may attend as audience members and ask questions about the research results.
Scheduled days for disputation
Mon 4 pm - 9 pm (lecture hall A)
Wed 4 pm - 9 pm (lecture hall A)
Thu 9 am - 2 pm (Lecture hall B)
Research Integrity
PhD positions and doctoral thesis
The topic of your doctoral thesis will be determined by the scientific focus of the research group in which you will take up your doctoral position. Please contact the individual research groups directly for information on open doctoral positions.

Habilitation - Qualification for University Teaching
What is the next step after a PhD program?
If you want to teach at a university, you should strive for a habilitation. Habilitation proves that a scientist can independently represent an academic field in research and teaching. For further information, please contact our habilitation office.
